message.content:
When you toss three fair coins, each coin can land either heads or tails.  
With three independent flips there are \(2^3 = 8\) equally‑likely outcomes:

| Outcome | Heads count |
|---------|-------------|
| HHH     | 3           |
| HHT     | 2           |
| HTH     | 2           |
| THH     | 2           |
| HTT     | 1           |
| THT     | 1           |
| TTH     | 1           |
| TTT     | 0           |

So the **possible numbers of heads** you can obtain are:

- **0 heads** (only one outcome – all tails)
- **1 head** (three outcomes – exactly one heads)
- **2 heads** (three outcomes – exactly two heads)
- **3 heads** (one outcome – all heads)

In other words, after tossing three coins you can get anywhere from 0 to 3 heads inclusive.
